every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal

claims.claim: Polar purine nucleoside analogs measured in fasted patients have absolute oral bioavailability above the 20% threshold: cladribine 36–46% and didanosine 22–28%.
Other polar nucleoside analogs with physicochemical profiles similar to the query show high oral bioavailability: lamivudine 69–87%, emtricitabine 92%, and zalcitabine 80%.
No supplied record provides affirmative evidence of F < 20% for a relevant nucleoside analog; the lowest relevant measured values are didanosine at 22–28%, still above the threshold.

evidence_gaps: No direct absolute oral bioavailability measurement for the query molecule is present in the supplied records.
The query prandial state is unspecified; most supporting records are fasted, and the fed cladribine record is less directly applicable.

Structural differences between the carbocyclic guanine nucleoside and the deoxyribose or oxathiolane nucleoside analogs could affect permeability or first-pass extraction, though all relevant analogs exceed the 20% threshold.
The physicochemical prior is mixed/unclear, with low logD and high TPSA suggesting possible permeability limitations, but this is not affirmative evidence for F < 20%.
